name: HEE Series Aluminium Frame Aquarium
summary: A large aluminium-framed tank on a matching cabinet, with a four-chamber sump hidden underneath and a DC return pump already fitted. It comes in two depths (60 and 73 cm front to back) across three lengths, so it is built for big display fish rather than a nano scape.
highlights: Six sizes from about 500 to 860 litres
Ultra-clear glass in an aluminium frame
JDP-10000 DC return pump and AQ smart controllers included
bestFor: Keepers planning a big community or large-fish display who want the filtration and plumbing sorted out of the box.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HJJ Series Home Aquarium
summary: A mid-size home aquarium set with a drawer-style sump in the cabinet, LED lighting in the lid and a CQB pump. The narrow 33 cm depth keeps it easy to fit against a wall, from a 70 litre starter up to about 230 litres.
highlights: Drawer-type four-stage bottom filter, easy to pull out and rinse
Front and rear glass flaps for feeding
Brushed silver, black or gold finish
bestFor: Someone after a tidy, ready-to-run fish tank for a living room with a modest footprint.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

specs.Filtration: Four-way drawer sump (1000 and 1200 add a sediment chamber)

extra.Filtration: New four-way bottom filter (drawer)+front separation sedimentation bin
New four-way bottom filter (drawer)+front separation sedimentation bin

name: ZEF Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a sump built into the stand, sold in three depths (35, 42 and 48 cm) and lengths from 60 cm to 2 m. The range is wide enough to find a size for most rooms, and every model comes with a lid light and CQB return pump.
highlights: AQ smart controllers in the lid and cabinet
Grey, blue or orange cabinet colours
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a sump tank in an exact size without building plumbing themselves.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HCB Rear Filter Aquarium
summary: A compact cube-ish tank on a matching stand, with the filter hidden in a rear compartment instead of a sump. It ships with an ADT spotlight on a stand, which gives it a more open, scape-friendly look than SunSun's lidded fish tanks.
highlights: Rear filter chamber with HQJ-700G pump
bestFor: A small open-top planted or nano fish tank where you want the filter out of sight.
watchOut: The included ADT-110C and 120C lights are modest (10 to 20 W), so fast carpeting plants may want more light.

specs.Colours: Red, blues, orange, turquoise, yellow, white

name: XHF Rear Filter Aquarium
summary: A small tank-and-stand set from SunSun's Xiaoli line with a filter chamber tucked behind the back glass. B models come with an LED light and glass flap lid; C models are the lower, lidless version.
highlights: Stand raised on a 10 cm bracket
bestFor: A neat first aquarium or bedroom tank where cables and filter should stay hidden.
watchOut: The rear chamber eats a little depth from the display area, so the scape is shallower than the outside size suggests.

name: HEZ Series All-in-One Aquarium
summary: One family covering everything from a 12 litre desktop tank to a 250 litre cabinet set. Small sizes use a top filter, the 800 to 1200 models a side filter, and the D versions add a sump in the stand.
highlights: Ultra-clear glass, 8 to 10 mm on the big models
Remote-controlled LED lighting and temperature display
bestFor: Beginners who want a complete kit and may want to size up later within the same look.
watchOut: Colour-changing lid LEDs suit fish display; for demanding plants you would add a proper planted light.

specs.Filtration: Top filter (300 to 600), side filter (800 to 1200), sump (D models)
specs.Also sold as: HEW series, and HE series for the 300 to 600 sizes

name: HYM-B Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A wood-effect cabinet aquarium with a compact sump underneath and HD glass on all four sides. Four lengths from 60 to 120 cm keep it in normal living-room territory.
highlights: Walnut, white or grey wood finishes
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a furniture-style tank with built-in filtration.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

specs.Lid: Front and rear glass flip cover

name: Stream Tank Series Aquarium
summary: A low, 45 cm tall tank on a cabinet, lit by one or two ADT-120C stand lights rather than a closed lid. The shallow height and open top make it one of SunSun's more aquascape-friendly cabinet sets.
highlights: Shallow 45 cm tank height, easy to reach the substrate
Open top with ADT-120C stand lighting
bestFor: Planted-tank keepers who want a shallow, open-top display on a matching stand.
watchOut: Two ADT-120C lights on the longer tanks is a low-to-medium light setup, fine for easy plants but not for high-tech carpets.

specs.Lighting: ADT-120C stand light (two on 1000 mm models)
specs.Styles: A, B and C cabinets share the same tank sizes

name: ZHA Series Aluminium Arowana Aquarium
summary: A heavy-duty aluminium tank designed for arowana and other large fish, with a deep sump and DC pump on the bigger sizes. At 49 to 61 cm deep and up to 2 m long, it is a serious piece of furniture.
highlights: ZZA LED bars and AQ controllers included
FD models add a sediment trap before the sump
bestFor: Large-fish keepers who need a big, sturdy tank more than a scaping canvas.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HLFT Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A broad cabinet-aquarium range with a sump below, offered in four depths from 35 to 60 cm. It keeps the same basic layout across 16 sizes, so it is easy to pick one to fit a specific wall.
bestFor: Fish keepers after a standard sump tank in a size that matches their space.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HMTX Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a sump, clear front and back glass and extra-clear side panels. It runs from 60 to 150 cm in two depths, with an HJ-2200 return pump across the range.
bestFor: A family tank where you want the filter and plumbing inside the cabinet.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

specs.Glass: Clear front and back, ultra-clear sides

name: HLF Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a sump and a noticeably brighter lid light than SunSun's similar HLFT range (20 to 46 W). Two depths and nine lengths from 60 to 150 cm.
highlights: Nine sizes from 90 to about 335 litres
Brighter LED lid lights than HLFT
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a sump tank with a bit more light for easy plants.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: Joy Series Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a small sump and a three-colour switchable LED lid. Four lengths from 80 to 150 cm, all with a CQB-2500 return pump.
bestFor: A colourful living-room fish tank where the kit is all included.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HRG-D Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: The cabinet version of SunSun's curved-front HRG tanks, with a small sump in the stand. It is a compact option from 50 to 100 cm long.
bestFor: Someone wanting a small sump tank with a softer, curved look.
watchOut: SunSun does not publish water volumes for this range, and dimensions are hand-measured (plus or minus 1 to 2 cm).

name: HMT Series Home Aquarium
summary: A tall, lidded cabinet aquarium with a sump and AQ smart controllers, sold in two depths from 60 to 150 cm. It is SunSun's everyday family-tank layout.
highlights: AQ-192H lid and AQ-130 cabinet controllers
bestFor: Households wanting a complete fish tank that looks like furniture.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HUM Series Bullet-Front Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a curved, bullet-style front glass and a sump underneath. Three lengths from 1 to 1.5 m, all 44 cm deep.
bestFor: Fish keepers who like a curved front and want a big tank without fuss.
watchOut: Curved glass distorts the view at the corners, which matters more for photographing a scape than for watching fish.

name: HAT Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A tall cabinet aquarium with an aluminium lifting lid, ultra-clear glass and a sump in the stand. Eight sizes in two depths, from 160 to 385 litres.
highlights: Gold apple, light wood or teak finish
bestFor: People who want a clearer-glass sump tank without going up to the largest sizes.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HST Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a touch-screen controller and one-touch drain, sold from 60 cm up to a 2 m, 740 litre display. Deeper models circulate water down both sides into the sump.
highlights: Teak, apple, gold wood grain or white walnut
bestFor: Keepers wanting a larger sump tank with some convenience features.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

specs.Filtration: Sump (dual-side overflow on ID, FD and AD models)
specs.Colours: Congo teak, golden apple, gold wood grain, white walnut

name: HWW Series Pipeless Aquarium
summary: A big display tank where the filtration runs without visible pipes in the tank, feeding a DC pump in the cabinet. It starts at 1.5 m and runs past 900 litres.
highlights: No visible pipework in the display
bestFor: Large display tanks where a clean, pipe-free look matters.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: H2TS Series Filter Aquarium
summary: A lidded cabinet tank that pairs a sump with an efficient JTP frequency pump on most sizes. It comes in three depths from 42 to 60 cm.
highlights: Low-power JTP pumps (18 to 25 W) on most models
Aluminium lifting lid and touch display
bestFor: Keepers wanting a big sump tank with lower running costs on the pump.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

specs.Colours: Yellow rosewood, red rosewood, gold wood grain, black

name: H3TS Series Barrel Filter Aquarium
summary: Instead of a sump, this cabinet tank runs its filtration through closed barrel-style filter buckets hidden in the stand, fed by an STP-3800 pump. A sealed setup like this loses less CO2 than a trickle sump, which matters if you plan to inject.
highlights: Closed barrel filters in the cabinet
bestFor: Keepers who want a cabinet tank with sealed filtration, including CO2-injected planted setups.

specs.Colours: Yellow rosewood, red rosewood, gold wood grain

name: H2G Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: SunSun's giant display range, from 1.8 m up to a 3 m long, 1,350 litre tank with a large sump and DC pump. Two depths, 61 and 74 cm.
highlights: Remote control and large touch screen
bestFor: Very large fish displays in homes or offices.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: H2FU Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a U-shaped baffle in the sump and a partition screen design, from 1 m to 2 m long. Five depth and size bands cover 191 to 922 litres.
bestFor: Fish keepers wanting a mid-to-large sump tank with plenty of sizing choice.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HYTX Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium range that mixes sump models (ED, ID, FD, AD) with IT models that use barrel filters instead. Sizes run from 1 m to 2 m.
highlights: IT models use sealed barrel filters
bestFor: Keepers who want the choice between a sump and sealed barrel filtration in the same cabinet style.
watchOut: Sump models trickle off injected CO2 quickly; pick an IT model if you plan to run CO2 for plants.

specs.Filtration: Sump (ED, ID, FD, AD) or barrel filters (IT)
specs.Colours: Wine red, BMW grey, pearl white

name: HFC Series Open-Top Aquarium
summary: An open-top tank on a matching cabinet, designed to run with an external canister (SunSun suggests the HW-302 or HW-303A). With no lid or built-in sump, it is the most scape-friendly of SunSun's cabinet sets.
highlights: 45 cm deep, good room for a layered scape
Open top for hanging or stand lights
bestFor: Planted-tank keepers who want a clean open tank and stand and prefer to pick their own canister and light.
watchOut: No light or filter included, so budget for both.

name: HEK Series Open Aquarium
summary: An open, ultra-clear glass tank sold with a slim ADP light on telescopic legs and an HBL hang-on filter. The 30 to 80 cm sizes line up with common aquascaping footprints.
highlights: ADP stand light and HBL hang-on filter included
Optional matching cabinet for 300 and 380 sizes
bestFor: A first planted nano or small scape where you want tank, light and filter in one purchase.
watchOut: The included lights are low wattage (2.5 to 8 W on the small sizes), so stick to easy, low-light plants or upgrade the light.

specs.Included: ADP or ADS light, HBL hang-on filter

name: ZHR Desktop Aquarium
summary: A 26 litre desktop tank with curved front corners, a lid light and a small pump-driven top filter. It is a simple all-included starter size.
bestFor: A desk or bedside tank for a few small fish or shrimp.

name: ZHE Desktop Aquarium
summary: A small ultra-clear desktop tank with a built-in top filter and colour-changing LED lid, run from a 12 V adapter. Three sizes from 13 to 46 litres; J versions differ in trim.
highlights: APJ pump and top filter included
bestFor: Nano fish or shrimp tanks on a desk.

name: HNE-380 Desktop Aquarium
summary: A 26 litre white desktop tank with twin 3 W colour-changing LEDs and an HQJ-500G pump. It runs on a 12 V adapter.
bestFor: A simple desk tank for small fish.
watchOut: SunSun gives no dimensions for this model, and the pump must stay submerged.

name: HRK Series Open Nano Aquarium
summary: Open-top ultra-clear tanks with curved (hot-bent) front corners and 5 mm glass, from a 3.5 litre pico up to 55 litres. Nothing is included, which leaves you free to choose light and filter.
bestFor: Nano scapes and shrimp tanks where you want an open top and your own choice of light and filter.
watchOut: Bent-glass corners distort the view slightly at the edges.

name: HRG Series Desktop Aquarium
summary: A range of curved-corner desktop tanks with a lid light and pump, from 29 to 80 cm long. The larger sizes are really small floor tanks without a cabinet.
highlights: Five sizes from 29 to 80 cm long
Single flat front, curved side edges
bestFor: Beginners who want a complete small tank.
watchOut: Sizes are hand-measured and include the lid and base, and SunSun's listed volumes for most sizes do not add up against those dimensions, so work out real capacity from the glass size.

specs.Glass: Hot-bent, flat front and curved edges

name: XHR Desktop Aquarium
summary: Curved-corner HD glass desktop tanks from 13 to 76 litres, each with a top circulation filter and 12 V LED. The HRX series shares the 300 and 380 sizes.
bestFor: A beginner or kids' tank on a desk or chest of drawers.

name: XHM Desktop Aquarium
summary: Two very small desktop tanks with a built-in JP-230G pump and 12 V light. They suit a betta or a few shrimp.
bestFor: A single betta or small shrimp colony on a desk.
watchOut: No volume is published, and the tank must sit fully flat with the pump submerged.

name: HR Series Desktop Aquarium
summary: Small HD glass desktop tanks with a rain-shower filter and flip-up feeding hatch, from 6 to 52 litres. White or black trim.
bestFor: A tidy starter tank for small fish.

name: HWK Series View Aquarium
summary: Ultra-clear open tanks on a removable base, matched with an HBL hang-on filter and ADP light (sold as a creative package). Seven sizes from 3.5 to 55 litres.
highlights: Matching HBL filter and ADP light
bestFor: Nano planted tanks and shrimp setups.

name: AT Series View Aquarium
summary: Desktop tanks with an integrated filter and eight-colour gradient LED, from 17 to 55 litres. B and C versions differ in style.
bestFor: A decorative fish tank on a desk or counter.
watchOut: The colour-cycling light is for show; plants will want a steady white light.

name: HSJ Waterview Aquarium
summary: A waterview tank with a raised land area and side filter, built for riparium or paludarium-style scapes. Four sizes from about 30 to 60 cm, all run by a small JP-230G pump.
highlights: Four sizes from 30.6 to 60.6 cm long
bestFor: Scapers wanting a ready-made land-and-water display.
watchOut: No water volume is given, and the 2.5 W pump is gentle for the larger sizes.

name: Small Aquarium Cabinet
summary: A plain storage cabinet sized to fit under SunSun's small HE, HEK and HSJ tanks. It stands 80 cm tall on 2 cm feet, with a hidden cupboard for food, scissors and test kits.
bestFor: Anyone putting a small SunSun tank on a stand instead of a desk.
watchOut: Sized for specific SunSun tanks; check your tank's footprint before buying.

name: ADT-I Nano Stand Light
summary: A small cylindrical LED spotlight hung from an arm that clamps to the tank rim, sized for nano and small tanks from 20 to 60 cm. SunSun ships it with several of its tanks, and it gives an open-top tank a clean, gallery look.
highlights: Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick
bestFor: Nano planted tanks and small shrimp setups with an open top.
watchOut: One puck light gives a pool of light rather than even coverage, so the edges of a wider tank stay dimmer.

specs.Mount: Clamp-on stand arm (T1 or T2 bracket)

name: ADT-2 Stand Light
summary: A cube-shaped LED spotlight on a rim-mounted arm, with vents on three sides for cooling. The 240C and 260C let you adjust brightness and colour temperature, covering tanks from 30 to 60 cm.
highlights: Two colour modes, adjustable on 240C and 260C
Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick
bestFor: Small open-top planted tanks where you want a strong, focused light.
watchOut: A single spotlight suits roughly cube-shaped tanks better than long, shallow ones.

name: ADT-3 Stand Light
summary: A larger aluminium spotlight for 40 to 80 cm tanks, with adjustable power and colour temperature and two switchable modes. It hangs from a T3 rim-mounted stand.
bestFor: Medium open-top planted tanks that need more punch than a nano light.
watchOut: Spotlights can leave the corners of a rectangular tank darker than the centre.

name: ADT-880C Panel Light
summary: A flat 58 × 30 cm LED panel held over the tank on two stand brackets, rated for tanks up to 120 cm. Power and colour temperature are adjustable up to 80 W.
bestFor: Open-top planted tanks where you want a wide, even spread from one fixture.
watchOut: At 58 cm long, a 120 cm tank will have darker ends; it works best on tanks near its own length.

name: ADT Round Clip Light
summary: A round 20 cm LED disc on a clamp arm, made in freshwater versions of 48 and 80 W. The 100C is the brighter 'glare' version for 60 to 80 cm tanks.
highlights: Clamps to glass up to 20 mm
bestFor: Mid-size open-top planted tanks where a single bright light is enough.
watchOut: SunSun also sells H (seawater) versions of this light; make sure you pick the C models for a planted tank.

name: ADP Slim LED Light
summary: A very slim (7 mm) LED bar on adjustable legs, in 11 lengths from 8 cm up to 110 cm. It is the light SunSun pairs with its HEK and HWK open tanks.
bestFor: Low-tech planted tanks, shrimp tanks and fish-only setups that want a neat, low-profile light.
watchOut: Output is low for the size (about 16 W on a 100 cm tank), so it is for easy, low-light plants only.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: ADE LED Light
summary: A slim 63 mm wide LED bar for tanks from about 28 to 113 cm, with more output per length than the ADP. Six sizes from 12 to 28 W.
highlights: Six sizes for tanks 28 to 113 cm
bestFor: Low to medium light planted tanks on a budget.
watchOut: Brightness does not scale much with length (28 W at 90 cm), so longer tanks get less light per litre.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: ADS LED Light
summary: A 10 cm wide LED bar for tanks from 38 to 130 cm, in fixed C7 aquatic versions and dimmable T versions. The larger C7 models reach 60 to 80 W.
highlights: C7 aquatic versions from 14 to 80 W
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks where you want a single bar with decent output.
watchOut: The H (sea light) versions in the same range are for marine tanks; pick C7 or T for plants.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: ADF LED Light
summary: A wide 22.5 cm LED panel-bar for big tanks from 70 to 150 cm, from 45 to 90 W. The width spreads light across deeper tanks better than a narrow strip.
highlights: Four sizes for tanks 70 to 150 cm
bestFor: Larger planted tanks that need a bright, wide light.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: AMD Hang-On Nano Light
summary: A tiny USB-powered (5 V) LED that hooks over thin glass, for nano tanks up to about 50 cm. The AD-150 is a small clip-on lamp for tanks under 30 cm.
bestFor: Betta tanks, pico scapes and shrimp cubes with easy plants.
watchOut: Only fits thin glass (5 mm or less) and is a low-light option.

name: ADZ Metal LED Spotlight
summary: A small metal-bodied mains LED spotlight (4.5 cm across) in 3, 5 and 7 W, with warm or three-colour adjustable white. It works as an accent light over an open nano tank.
bestFor: Accent lighting on a small open-top nano, or picking out a focal stone or plant alongside a main light.
watchOut: SunSun gives no mounting details or tank sizing, so plan how you will hang or aim it.

name: Dream White Plant Tube Light
summary: A sealed tube light from SunSun's Dream range, in the white version made for aquatic plants. It comes in six lengths for tanks from 80 cm to 2 m.
bestFor: Large tanks that already have a lid and want a simple plant-oriented tube.
watchOut: Output is low for the tank sizes it targets (30 W for 2 m), so treat it as a supplement or for undemanding plants.

name: ZDO Amphibious Tube Light
summary: A sealed LED tube that can run in or out of water, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, for tanks from 1.2 m upward. Four lengths from 98 to 170 cm.
bestFor: Big lidded fish tanks that want extra or replacement lighting.
watchOut: Low output for such long tanks; it will not drive a demanding planted setup on its own.

name: HW-3000 Series Frequency Canister Filter
summary: SunSun's variable-speed canister, with a touch display that steps the pump through six or seven flow levels and a built-in 9 W UV-C lamp. An oil-film skimmer comes with it to clear surface scum.
highlights: 1,200 to 4,600 L/h depending on model and setting
bestFor: Large planted or community tanks (roughly 200 litres and up) where adjustable flow is useful.
watchOut: These are big units (up to 55 cm tall and 10.5 kg on the HW-5000), so check your cabinet height first.

specs.Control: LED touch screen for flow and UV timer

name: HW-700 Series Canister Filter
summary: A three-size canister range from 1,000 to 2,000 L/h, each sold as an A version (no UV) or B version with a 9 W UV-C lamp. It is SunSun's current take on the popular HW-300 series.
bestFor: Mid to large planted tanks, roughly 150 to 500 litres, on a budget.
watchOut: Budget canisters vary in seal quality; check the lid O-ring when setting up and after cleaning.

bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks where you want a simple canister.

summary: An external filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line with stacked media trays (three or five tiers) and an optional 9 W UV-C lamp. Flow runs from 500 to 1,400 L/h.

name: HBL Series Hang-On Filter
summary: SunSun's long-running hang-on-back filters, from the tiny 2 W HBL-301 up to the larger adjustable-flow HBL-800 range. They are cheap, simple and easy to service.
highlights: HBL-801 to 803 have adjustable flow and fit different glass thicknesses
Used in several SunSun tank kits
bestFor: Nano and small planted tanks, shrimp tanks and quarantine setups.
watchOut: Hang-on filters break the surface and can drive off CO2, and the intake needs a sponge cover in a shrimp tank.

name: CBG Hang-On Filter with UV
summary: A hang-on-back filter with an oil-film surface skimmer, double flow regulation and a built-in 5 W UV-C lamp (S models skip the UV). Two sizes for 38 to 190 litre tanks.
bestFor: Small to mid planted tanks that suffer from surface film or green water.
watchOut: UV kills free-floating algae but will not fix algae on plants or glass; the root cause still needs sorting.

name: XBL Hang-On Filter
summary: A small hang-on filter from SunSun's Xiaoli line, in four sizes for tanks up to 30, 40, 50 and 60 cm. Flow is 300 or 500 L/h.
highlights: Sized by tank length (30 to 60 cm)
bestFor: Nano and small tanks under 60 cm.

name: XBA Clip-On Filter
summary: A very small 2.5 W clip-on filter with an activated carbon plate, for tanks under 40 cm. Flow is up to 300 L/h.
bestFor: Pico and nano tanks, betta setups.
watchOut: Carbon removes liquid fertiliser too, so swap it for sponge in a planted tank.

name: AF-260 Top Filter
summary: A top-mounted filter box for tanks 30 to 60 cm long that sits on the rim and takes 14/16 mm hose from a pump. It gives a small tank a trickle-style media box without a sump.
bestFor: Small fish tanks where you want extra media above the water.
watchOut: Trickle boxes vent CO2, so it is not ideal for an injected planted tank.

name: JS Three-in-One Top Filter
summary: A rim-mounted top filter box with its own pump, whose support arms extend to fit different tank widths. Two sizes, 350 and 650 L/h.
highlights: Adjustable arms (24 to 41 cm, or 41 to 61 cm)
Filter box sold separately as JS-400B/600B
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks that want easy-access top filtration.
watchOut: Like any trickle filter, it drives off CO2 and splashes more than a canister.

name: JF Biochemical Sponge Filter
summary: A twin sponge filter driven by a small 3 W electric pump instead of an air pump, in three widths. It gives gentle flow and a big sponge surface for bacteria.
bestFor: Shrimp tanks, fry tanks and small planted tanks that need gentle, safe filtration.

name: HN Internal Filter
summary: A slim 3 W internal filter for small tanks, with 300 L/h flow. Two heights.
bestFor: Nano and small tanks up to about 40 litres.

name: XN Low Water Level Filter
summary: An internal filter built to work in shallow water, with one, two or three stacked media sections. Every size runs the same 10 W, 800 L/h pump.
bestFor: Shallow tanks and low water levels where a normal internal filter would suck air.

name: HJ-42 Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ submersible pumps fitted with a sponge filter chamber, from 400 to 3,000 L/h. They can filter a tank on their own or push water through a separate filter.
bestFor: Small to large fish tanks and temporary setups.
watchOut: The bigger models make strong, noisy flow for their size; the small ones suit planted tanks better.

name: HJ-B Series Mini Internal Filter
summary: Tiny internal filters from 200 L/h, plus a few larger HJ-5x2 models up to 1,200 L/h. Several are used in SunSun's desktop tanks.
bestFor: Pico, nano and small tanks.

name: JP-F Series Internal Filter
summary: SunSun's JP submersible pumps with tall sponge filter columns attached, from 300 to 1,600 L/h. The JP-02x/B versions are the same pump sizes sold without the filter column.
bestFor: Small to mid fish tanks.

name: JP-09 Series Internal Filter
summary: Three small internal filters from 250 to 650 L/h, drawing only 3 to 7 W.
bestFor: Small tanks that need low-wattage internal filtration.

name: HQJ-I and HQJ-S Internal Filter
summary: Internal filters with a sponge column and pump head, from 300 to 500 L/h. The S versions of the 700 and 900 carry a much taller filter section than the I versions.
bestFor: Small fish tanks and quarantine tanks.

name: XQP-F Internal Filter
summary: The Xiaoli-line version of SunSun's filter pumps, with a filter box on the intake, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. The same pumps are sold bare as the XQP water pumps.
bestFor: Small to mid tanks.

name: CHJ-02 Series Internal Filter
summary: CHJ pumps fitted with a clear media column, from 500 to 1,500 L/h. Handy as a simple all-in-one internal filter.
bestFor: Small and mid fish tanks.

name: CF Series Internal Filter Pump
summary: A simple internal filter pump in three sizes, 350 to 900 L/h. SunSun lists flow, head and power but no dimensions.
bestFor: Small fish tanks.

name: JUP UV Internal Filter
summary: An internal filter with a UV-C lamp built into the body, from 500 to 800 L/h. Lamp sizes run from 5 to 13 W.
bestFor: Tanks fighting green water that want the UV inside the tank.
watchOut: UV clears green water but will not fix nutrient or light problems causing algae on plants.

name: CUP-800 UV Internal Filter
summary: A compact internal filter pump with a UV-C lamp built in. SunSun rates the UV for 250 to 750 litres depending on lamp size, but every model pumps the same 700 L/h.
bestFor: Mid to large tanks with green water problems.
watchOut: Flow is modest for the tank sizes quoted, so treat it as a UV unit rather than main filtration on big tanks.

name: AUV UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp that sits in the tank or sump, from 3 to 14 W, rated for 500 to 2,600 litres. Most sizes come with a shade to block visible glare.
highlights: Rated for up to 500 to 2,600 litres
Light shield on 6 W and up
bestFor: Tanks or sumps with green water or where you want to cut free-floating bacteria.
watchOut: UV-C can harm eyes and degrade some plastics; never look at the lit lamp and keep it shielded.

name: ZUV Timer UV-C Lamp
summary: A submersible UV-C lamp with a built-in timer, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, rated for 1,800 to 2,600 litres. Three sizes, 10 to 14 W.
highlights: Rated for up to 1,800 to 2,600 litres
bestFor: Large tanks and sumps with green water.
watchOut: Keep the lamp shielded and switched off when your hands are in the tank.

name: JY Surface Skimmer
summary: A small powered surface skimmer that draws the top layer of water through a floating intake to clear oily film. Two versions at 300 L/h.
bestFor: Planted tanks with surface film that blocks gas exchange and light.

name: ZTB Aquarium Heater
summary: An adjustable heater from SunSun's Zhizhen line, from 50 to 1,000 W, with a 20 to 35 °C range. SunSun rates each size by tank volume.
bestFor: Any freshwater tank, sized to its volume.

name: YRB-800 Electronic Heater
summary: An electronic heater with an external controller that holds temperature to about 1 °C and remembers its setting after a power cut. Also sold as the ZRB series.
bestFor: Mid to large tanks where you want to set and read temperature outside the water.

name: YRB-900 Aquarium Heater
summary: An adjustable heater range from a small 30 W up to 500 W, sized by tank length. It is short for its power (18 to 28 cm).
bestFor: Nano to large tanks.

name: JRB Aquarium Heater
summary: A classic adjustable glass heater in 100 to 500 W sizes, plus the YRB-065, a small preset heater fixed at 26 °C. Sized by tank length.
bestFor: Everyday tropical tanks.

name: YRB-250 Remote Heater
summary: A 500 W heater with an external controller and remote control, for 100 to 120 cm tanks. The ARB-250 is the same heater in a different finish.
bestFor: Large tanks where you want to check and set temperature easily.

name: AR Series Aquarium Heater
summary: A broad range of adjustable heaters from 50 to 1,000 W: compact AR-2 units and flat AR-3 heaters for bigger tanks and sumps. Rated from 20 to 900 litres.
bestFor: Any size tank, including sumps that need a lot of heat.

name: ARB Digital Heater
summary: A high-power heater (500 to 1,000 W) with a separate digital display controller, remote and thermistor probe. Built for 300 to 900 litre tanks.
bestFor: Large display tanks and sumps.

name: XRB Intelligent Heater
summary: A 600 or 1,000 W heater with an external controller, from SunSun's Xiaoli line, for 300 to 900 litre tanks.
bestFor: Large tanks and sumps.

name: HYH-D Aquarium Chiller
summary: The smallest units in SunSun's HYH chiller range, with 250 to 650 W of cooling for tanks around 260 to 580 litres. They take 16 to 20 mm hose and use R134a refrigerant.
bestFor: Tanks in hot rooms or with cool-water species that climb above safe temperatures in summer.
watchOut: Chillers need a pump or canister to push water through and dump heat into the room, so give them ventilation.

specs.Bigger units: HYH DR models cover 800 to 4,500 litres

name: AK Series Automatic Feeder
summary: Small automatic feeders that clamp to the tank rim or stand on a base, with battery, USB or WiFi (smart) versions. Hoppers hold 50 to 100 g of food.
highlights: WiFi app control on AK-03 and AK-23
bestFor: Holidays and busy weeks, for tanks with fish that eat flake or pellets.
watchOut: Automatic feeders can clump in humid air over the tank; test one for a few days before leaving it.

specs.Power: 2 × AA batteries, or 5 V USB on some models

extra.Mount: Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm
Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm
Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm
Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm
Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm
Base or clamp, glass 3 to 20 mm

name: ZK Series Automatic Feeder
summary: A drum-style automatic feeder from SunSun's Zhizhen line, in a simple battery version and a smart version with app control. Feeding runs on 8, 12 or 24 hour cycles.
bestFor: Keepers who want phone control of feeding while away.

name: HXS Electric Gravel Cleaner
summary: A battery or mains powered gravel washer that sucks debris out of the substrate and returns filtered water, or pumps water out for a change. Four versions from 350 to 1,000 L/h.
highlights: Sand washing and water pumping modes
bestFor: Fish tanks with sand or gravel, and planted tanks with an inert substrate cap.
watchOut: Keep it away from soft aqua soil, which it will suck up and break down.

name: AX Electric Water Changer
summary: A submersible pump with a rigid pipe and duckbill intake for water changes and sand washing. Three pump sizes, each with a 2 m or 5 m cable.
bestFor: Regular water changes on mid and large tanks.

name: ZL Magnetic Glass Cleaner
summary: A magnetic glass cleaner in four strengths for glass from 3 to 29 mm, with a scraper blade on all but the smallest. Sized by tank length.
highlights: Four sizes for glass 3 to 29 mm
Suits tanks up to and over 120 cm
bestFor: Keeping the front glass clear without getting your hands wet.
watchOut: Grit caught under the pad or blade will scratch glass; wipe it first and never use it on acrylic.

name: HJ-41 Series Submersible Pump
summary: A long-running line of compact AC submersible pumps from 400 to 3,000 L/h, with a round intake cover. Useful for powering a DIY filter, a return from a small sump or a water-change setup.
bestFor: Small sumps, DIY filters and general water moving.
watchOut: Older AC design, so power use is high for the flow on the bigger models; DC pumps are quieter and adjustable.

name: HJ Series Submersible Pump
summary: SunSun's HJ-500 to HJ-6000 pumps, a common choice as sump return pumps in its own cabinet tanks. Ten sizes from 500 to 6,800 L/h.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed-loop circulation on mid to large tanks.
watchOut: The large models are power hungry (150 W for the HJ-6000); a DC or frequency pump will cost less to run.

name: HJ Mini Submersible Pump
summary: Tiny pumps from 200 to 800 L/h, used in desktop tanks, small fountains and DIY nano filters. The smallest are under 4 cm across.
bestFor: Nano tanks, all-in-one rear chambers and small DIY projects.

name: JP-06 Series Submersible Pump
summary: Multi-purpose AC pumps from 450 to 3,800 L/h with a boxy body and wide outlet sizes. Eight sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering external filters on mid-size tanks.
watchOut: Power draw is high on the large models compared with SunSun's frequency pumps.

name: JP-GL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump that can draw water down to about 5 mm, with a ceramic shaft and a 360 degree intake. Five sizes from 600 to 1,600 L/h.
highlights: Pumps down to about 5 mm of water
bestFor: Shallow sumps and emptying tanks during water changes.

name: JP-G Series Submersible Pump
summary: Compact pumps from the 250 L/h JP-230G used in many SunSun desktop tanks, up to 1,800 L/h. The GS versions are rated a little differently from the G pump of the same size, so compare flow and head model by model.
bestFor: Nano tank filters, small sumps and DIY builds.

name: JQP Submersible Pump and Filter
summary: An efficient compact pump range from 500 to 3,500 L/h, sold bare or with a filter column (JQP-F). Up to 3.6 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to mid tanks.

specs.F models: The F models add a filter sponge on the intake so the pump works as a simple internal filter

name: XQP Submersible Pump
summary: Compact Xiaoli-line pumps in 500, 1,000 and 1,500 L/h, also sold with a filter box as XQP-F. Low wattage for the flow.
bestFor: Small sumps, rear-chamber tanks and DIY filters.

name: HQJ and CQJ Submersible Pump
summary: Small pumps from 350 to 1,600 L/h in several body styles, including 12 V DC versions (HQJ-D). The HQJ-500G and 700G are fitted to many SunSun tanks.
bestFor: Desktop and small tank filtration, rear chambers and top filters.

name: CHJ Multi-Function Pump
summary: A broad range of AC pumps from 500 to 6,000 L/h. The CHJ-02 versions come with a filter column.
bestFor: Sump returns and powering filters on tanks of most sizes.

name: XGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A pump with a thermal cut-out against running dry, a 360 degree intake and the ability to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 500 to 3,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and shallow sumps.

name: JGP Low Water Level Pump
summary: A bottom-intake pump with dry-run protection and a ceramic shaft, able to pump down to about 5 mm. Six sizes from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h.
bestFor: Water changes and draining tanks, shallow sumps.
watchOut: High wattage for the flow (130 W on the largest), so better for occasional jobs than 24/7 use.

name: ZHL Low Water Level Pump
summary: A carry-handle pump with a 360 degree bottom intake and dry-run protection, from 1,000 to 4,500 L/h. SunSun also sells it as the CHL series.
bestFor: Water changes, tank moves and draining.
watchOut: Built for moving water rather than running quietly all day.

name: JHP DC Pump
summary: A vertical 24 V DC pump from 2,000 to 6,000 L/h, with a slim cylindrical body. It fits tight sump sections.
bestFor: Sump returns where space is tight.

name: JDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: SunSun's popular 24 V DC return pump with a controller that steps flow through five levels on the bigger models. Seven sizes from 1,000 to 18,000 L/h; Q versions add a one-touch feed pause.
bestFor: Sump returns and closed loops where you want adjustable, quiet flow.

name: XDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A Xiaoli-line 24 V DC pump from 1,000 to 6,800 L/h. S versions push harder against head.
bestFor: Sump returns and filter feeds on small to large tanks.

name: CDP DC Frequency Pump
summary: A 24 V DC pump with an external controller, from 3,500 to 10,000 L/h. SunSun also sells the same pump as SDP and ZDP.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

extra.Variants: CDP-3500B (no controller) and CDP-3500W (WiFi)
CDP-6000B (no controller) and CDP-6000W (WiFi)
CDP-10000B (no controller) and CDP-10000W (WiFi)

name: JTP Frequency Pump
summary: Efficient frequency-controlled pumps from 1,800 to 5,800 L/h (including 12/24 V DC models) plus the smaller JTP-2000 to 3000. They move a lot of water for their wattage.
bestFor: Sump returns where running cost matters.

name: JTP-R Frequency Pump
summary: The larger JTP range, from 4,000 to 16,000 L/h, for big sumps and closed loops. Wattage stays reasonable for the flow.
bestFor: Large display tanks with a sump.
watchOut: Far too much flow for most planted tanks unless you are running a big sump.

name: CTP Frequency Pump
summary: A frequency pump range from 3,000 to 16,000 L/h, with low wattage for its flow. Twelve sizes.
bestFor: Sump returns on large tanks.

name: CTB Frequency Pump
summary: An efficient pump range from 2,500 to 7,000 L/h, suited to sumps and filter feeds. Six sizes.
bestFor: Mid to large sump returns.

name: STP Eco Pump
summary: An efficient pump that works submerged or dry-mounted, from 3,000 to 8,000 L/h. The STP-3800 drives the barrel filters in SunSun's H3TS and HYTX-IT tanks.
bestFor: Sump returns and driving external pressure filters.

name: ZSP Frequency Pump
summary: A Zhizhen-line frequency pump from 2,500 to 14,000 L/h. Ten sizes, up to 7 m head.
bestFor: Sump returns on mid to large tanks.

name: JVP Wavemaker
summary: SunSun's classic magnet-mount wavemakers, from a tiny 2,000 L/h unit to the 24,000 L/h twin-head JVP-402. The head can be aimed, and several models rotate on the magnet.
bestFor: Adding circulation to large planted tanks so CO2 and nutrients reach every plant.
watchOut: Pick a small one for a planted tank; too much flow flattens stems and blows substrate around.

name: XVP Wavemaker
summary: A Xiaoli-line magnet-mount wavemaker in three sizes from 2,500 to 12,000 L/h.
bestFor: Circulation in mid to large tanks.

name: XVA Wave Pump
summary: A submersible wave pump for glass up to 12 mm, from 6,000 to 10,000 L/h, with a ceramic shaft and a head that turns through 180 degrees. Each size also comes as an E version.
bestFor: Circulation in tanks up to about a metre.

name: CW Wavemaker
summary: A 24 V propeller wavemaker with an external controller, from 4,000 to 20,000 L/h. Standard models are adjustable across a wide range; S models run at a fixed rate.
bestFor: Planted tanks from 50 cm up that need gentle, adjustable circulation.

name: ZZP Cross-Flow Wave Pump
summary: A long, gyre-style cross-flow pump (29 cm) that produces a wide sheet of flow, with a separate 24 V controller. One size for 70 to 120 cm tanks.
bestFor: Larger planted tanks where you want broad, even flow instead of a jet.

name: YT AC/DC Rechargeable Air Pump
summary: Mains air pumps with a built-in rechargeable battery that takes over in a power cut, for about 8 hours (12 on the YT-8000). The range runs from the small twin-outlet YT-8000 to 100 L/min fish-room units.
bestFor: Backup aeration for fish rooms and big tanks where a power cut is a real risk.
watchOut: Most sizes are far larger than a planted tank needs; the YT-8000 is the one to look at for a home aquarium.

specs.Battery: Built in, about 8 h run time (12 h on YT-8000)

name: CQ-B Rechargeable Air Pump
summary: A mains air pump with an 8.4 V, 4000 mAh battery built in, in 12 and 16 L/min versions. It keeps air running during a power cut.
bestFor: Larger tanks and fish rooms that need backup aeration.

name: CP Series Air Pump
summary: SunSun's quiet low-power air pumps, many drawing just 1.5 W, from 1.5 L/min up to the 16 L/min CP-1000. The CP-202 and CP-402 are also sold as the ZP series.
bestFor: Sponge filters and air stones in nano and small tanks, and shrimp racks.
watchOut: Planted tanks with CO2 injection usually want air only at night, so pair it with a timer.

name: CIP Series Air Pump
summary: Small mains air pumps from 1.5 L/min single outlet to 5 L/min twin outlet, with adjustable output. The CIP-400 has thicker, sound-insulated walls.
bestFor: Sponge filters and air stones in small tanks.

name: CQ and CRP Series Air Pump
summary: A range of mains air pumps from a 1.7 L/min single outlet up to 30 L/min, plus the four-outlet CRP-600. CQ-200 and CQ-3000 are also sold as ZQ models.
bestFor: Anything from a single sponge filter to a small rack of tanks.

name: ZQ Air Pump
summary: Two Zhizhen-line air pumps: the twin-outlet 3.3 L/min ZQ-200 and the stronger 30 L/min ZQ-3000.
bestFor: Small tanks (ZQ-200) or several tanks from one pump (ZQ-3000).

name: CT Series Air Pump
summary: Copper-motor air pumps with a shock-absorbing body and adjustable output, from 1.5 L/min to four outlets at 2.8 L/min each. Most can hang on a wall hook.
bestFor: Sponge filters and air stones in small and mid tanks.

name: YT, HP and HT Magnetic Air Pump
summary: SunSun's vibration air pumps: small YT models from 1.5 L/min, the four-outlet YT-304 and HP-1116, and big HT units up to 75 L/min for fish rooms.
bestFor: From single small tanks (YT) to fish rooms (HT).

name: DY and HDY Electromagnetic Air Pump
summary: Linear diaphragm air pumps from 20 to 50 L/min, efficient for their output. The HJZ-30 in the range can also run from 12 V DC.
highlights: HJZ-30 runs on 220 V AC or 12 V DC
bestFor: Fish rooms and shrimp racks running many sponge filters from one pump.
watchOut: Overkill for one planted tank; a small CP or CT pump is plenty.

name: ZN-30 AC/DC Air Pump
summary: A 30 L/min electromagnetic air pump that runs on mains or a 12 V DC battery, so it can keep going during a power cut.
bestFor: Backup aeration for fish rooms and large tanks.
watchOut: You supply the 12 V battery; it is not built in.
